ours-net.short: Night School's small network, built for this film
ours-net.citation: media/school/backprop/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_backprop.mjs from system/school/backprop.mjs: a 2, 8, 8, 2 tanh network (114 numbers) on seeded two spirals, with a hand-written forward and backward pass and a finite-difference check of every number.
claims: Counted multiply-adds for one point: forward 98, backward 208 (ratio 2.12); tanh, exp and log calls counted apart.

Finite-difference check of every number: worst tensor error 1.2e-9 after training; worst single entry 3.3e-8. With the second hidden layer's local slope written as 1 - a instead of 1 - a^2, the check fails for W1, b1, W2 and b2 and passes for W3 and b3.
Held-out accuracy on 400 points, measured every 100 steps: 0.355 at the start, 0.95 reached by step 2,000, 0.9975 after 4,000 steps.
ours-net.n: 400 training and 400 held-out points; one seed.
ours-net.does_not_prove: Anything about large networks; one seed, one task.

linnainmaa1970.short: Linnainmaa 1970, reverse-mode accumulation of rounding errors
linnainmaa1970.citation: Linnainmaa, S. (1970). The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of the local rounding errors. Master's thesis, University of Helsinki.
linnainmaa1970.read: thesis not read (in Finnish); read Griewank 2012, Documenta Mathematica Extra Volume ISMP, 389-400, and Schmidhuber's history page
claims: Linnainmaa's 1970 thesis described what is now called reverse-mode automatic differentiation, for the accumulated rounding error of an algorithm; it was published in English in 1976, and the idea was also found independently by others, among them Werbos (1982) for networks.
linnainmaa1970.does_not_prove: That the method was then used to train neural networks.

rumelhart1986.short: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams 1986, Learning representations by back-propagating errors
rumelhart1986.citation: Rumelhart, D. E., Hinton, G. E., Williams, R. J. (1986). Learning representations by back-propagating errors. Nature 323, 533-536.
rumelhart1986.read: abstract only, and Schmidhuber's history page
claims: The paper describes back-propagation for networks of neuron-like units and shows that hidden units come to represent useful features of the task.
rumelhart1986.does_not_prove: That it was the first description of reverse-mode differentiation.

griewank2008.citation: Griewank, A., Walther, A. (2008). Evaluating Derivatives: Principles and Techniques of Algorithmic Differentiation, 2nd edition. SIAM.
griewank2008.read: book not read (paywalled); read Griewank 2012, which bounds the cost of the gradient by a small constant times the cost of the function (3 for multiplication counts)
claims: Reverse mode computes the gradient of a scalar function at a cost bounded by a small constant times the cost of the function, whatever the number of inputs. Our count of 2.12 is the backward pass alone; forward plus backward is 3.12 times the forward pass.
griewank2008.does_not_prove: The exact constant for a given program; we measured ours.

ours-model.short: Night School's tiny transformer, the attention lesson's trained weights
ours-model.citation: media/school/attention/model.json; system/school/backprop-attention.mjs checks tinyformer's hand-written backward pass by central differences.
claims: On 36 entries over 9 tensors, two held-out rows: worst relative error 2.9e-7 in float64; a control that drops the softmax Jacobian term fails 18 of 36.
This model trains with AdamW, a warmup and gradient clipping, not plain gradient descent.
ours-model.does_not_prove: That every entry is right; 36 of 20,864 were checked here (the lab's own test checks every tensor on a small model).
